record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.context_brief: Closure in pointwise and Zariski-type topologies
record.original_question: Describe: (1) transformation semigroups that are closed in the pointwise topology; and (2) endomorphism semigroups that are closed in a Zariski-type topology.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.15. (G. Mashevitzky)

    (1) Describe transformation semigroups that are closed in the pointwise topology.
    (2) Describe endomorphism semigroups that are closed in a topology of Zarisky type.

Motivation and definitions can be found in [6], [16], [17], [18]. Transformation semigroups closed in
the pointwise topology are precisely the semigroups of endomorphisms of mathematical structures
(see [18]). It was shown in [16] that the Zariski-type topology is weaker than the pointwise topology
and conditions were obtained under which these topologies coincide. Several special cases of the
problem were solved in [18].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a nonempty set and let $T(X)$ denote the full transformation monoid on $X$, i.e. the set of all maps $X \to X$ under composition. Endow $T(X)$ with the pointwise convergence topology: a net $(f_\alpha)$ converges to $f$ if and only if $f_\alpha(x) = f(x)$ eventually for every $x \in X$. Equivalently, $T(X)$ carries the product topology inherited from $X^X$ where $X$ is given the discrete topology. A subsemigroup $S \subseteq T(X)$ is said to be closed in the pointwise topology if it is closed as a subset of $T(X)$ in this topology. It is known that the closed subsemigroups of $T(X)$ in the pointwise topology are exactly the endomorphism monoids of relational (or first-order) structures with universe $X$.

Now let $\mathcal{A}$ be an algebraic structure (e.g. a group, semigroup, ring, or universal algebra), and let $\mathrm{End}(\mathcal{A})$ be its monoid of endomorphisms. The Zariski-type topology on $\mathrm{End}(\mathcal{A})$ is the topology whose subbasis of closed sets consists of the "equation solution sets"
$$V(u,v) = \{\, \varphi \in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{A}) : u(\varphi(a_1),\ldots,\varphi(a_n)) = v(\varphi(a_1),\ldots,\varphi(a_n))\,\},$$
where $u, v$ are terms in the signature of $\mathcal{A}$ and $a_1,\ldots,a_n \in \mathcal{A}$. The Zariski-type topology is in general weaker than the pointwise convergence topology on $\mathrm{End}(\mathcal{A})$.

Solve the following two problems.

(1) Give an intrinsic description (e.g. in terms of algebraic, combinatorial or model-theoretic invariants) of those subsemigroups of $T(X)$ that are closed in the pointwise convergence topology.

(2) Give an intrinsic description of those submonoids of $\mathrm{End}(\mathcal{A})$ (for $\mathcal{A}$ ranging over a natural class of algebraic structures) that are closed in the Zariski-type topology defined above.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed by G. Mashevitzky as part of a recent collection of unsolved semigroup-theoretic problems. Although several special cases have been settled (notably the characterization of pointwise-closed transformation semigroups as endomorphism monoids of relational structures, and partial coincidence results between Zariski and pointwise topologies for ω-categorical structures and for certain monoids/clones), no full intrinsic description in either part is available. Recent works (e.g. on Zariski topology on endomorphism monoids of ω-categorical structures, and on automatic continuity/unique Polish topologies for monoids) treat related fragments but leave the general descriptive problem open.

status_evidence.title: On the Zariski topology on endomorphism monoids of omega-categorical structures
status_evidence.snippet: For all concrete endomorphism monoids of ω-categorical structures on which the Zariski topology has been analysed thus far, the two topologies were shown to coincide.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial coincidence results between Zariski and pointwise topologies are known, and the general description remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Topologies of pointwise convergence in the first order languages and in affine spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Mashevitzky compared these topologies with Stone and Zariski topologies, showing the Zariski topology is strictly weaker than pointwise convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Mashevitzky has obtained partial structural results but no general description.

status_evidence.title: Automatic continuity, unique Polish topologies, and Zariski topologies on monoids and clones
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Zariski topologies on monoids and clones, including endomorphism monoids.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity addresses related fragments but does not resolve the descriptive problem.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Zariski topology on groups and semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results on Zariski topology on semigroups.
status_evidence.claim: Continued research indicates the problem is still under active investigation.
